comment: The AI ladder's players (D318): a name, an AI kind and its parameters. A name is permanent: never edit the kind or params of a player that has played (the ladder keys results by name AND config hash, so an edit would split it in two); add a new name instead. Anchors are stock Forge and are always in the pool; forge-default is fixed at 1500. tools/ai-ladder/kinds.ts lists the kinds and their parameters. `ai-ladder.sh tune` appends here and never overwrites.

players.name: forge-default
players.note: Forge 2.0.14's AI, Default.ai profile. The rating scale's zero: 1500.

players.name: forge-reckless
players.note: Reckless.ai; D311 measured it about +10 points over Default on the cube pairs.

players.name: forge-experimental
players.note: Experimental.ai: 30 knob values, not simulation (D311).

players.name: policy-outlet
players.note: D310's sacrifice-outlet policy in front of the Default AI.

players.name: search-v1
players.note: The game's `MtgTable --ai-policy search` seat with its defaults until D412: D310's outlet policy plus D312's determinized rollout search (D312-D314). Wall-clock budget: for live play, and machine-dependent as a benchmark. Since D412 the live seat is search-v2, the player search-v1-anytime; `--ai-search anytime=0` is this one.

players.name: search-v1-fixed3
players.note: Fixed-rollout benchmark mode: exactly 3 rounds per searched decision (search-v1 averaged ~2.5 on the shared container at 1.5 s), a fixed determinization seed, no budget fallback. Use this one for ladder, SPRT and tuner numbers that must reproduce across machines.

players.name: search-v1-fixed3-aturns1
players.note: D351 (engine review H1(c)): search-v1-fixed3 with ATTACK rollouts played to the end of the NEXT turn (aturns=1), so an attack sees the crack-back; every other decision keeps turns=0. Night 2's SPRT against search-v1-fixed3.

players.name: search-v1-fixed3-lcb
players.note: D350 (engine review M1): search-v1-fixed3 overriding Forge only when the paired difference's lower bound mean_d - 1*se_d clears 0 (3 rounds), instead of the raw mean beating Forge's by 20. Night 2's SPRT against search-v1-fixed3.

players.name: search-v1-fixed3-oracle
players.note: D350 (engine review M5): TEST ONLY -- search-v1-fixed3 whose rollouts keep the REAL hidden cards (no determinization). An upper bound on what inferring the opponent's hand could be worth; never a live seat (MtgTable refuses oracle=1), never rated by `run` unless named, never a league candidate. Night 2's SPRT against search-v1-fixed3.

players.name: search-v1-anytime
players.note: D388 (engine review, week 3): search-v1 with the anytime search -- a round the 1.5 s budget cuts keeps its rollouts, candidates are pruned to what the time left can carry, clearly worse ones are raced out, and the verdict is taken on whatever paired evidence exists (Forge's answer without a verdict only when no alternative was scored). Wall-clock by design: it is the budget behaviour being measured. SPRT against search-v1. D412 (J102's fixed match, ADOPT: 0.5133 [0.5036, 0.5230] against search-v1, budget fallbacks 0.7% vs 5.6%): this config is search-v2, the live `MtgTable --ai-policy search` seat's default (SearchConfig.LIVE_VERSION); the name stays, as every ladder name does.

players.name: search-v1-fixed3-ranked
players.note: D389 (week 3): search-v1-fixed3 generating up to 24 candidates and keeping Forge's, pass and the best 4 others by a one-step prior (each applied once on a shared determinization, the leaf after it) instead of the first 6 in enumeration order. SPRT against search-v1-fixed3.

players.name: search-v1-fixed3-routlets
players.note: D390 (week 3): search-v1-fixed3 whose rollouts play the searching seat with D310's sacrifice-outlet policy in front of Forge instead of plain Forge, so sacrifice lines are valued as the seat would play them. SPRT against search-v1-fixed3.

players.name: search-v1-reckless
players.note: D398 (the outside review's T5): search-v1 with Forge's Reckless.ai as the base profile instead of Default -- the seat's own answers, and its side of every rollout (the copy keeps the seat's lobby player, so its profile), are Reckless; every search knob is search-v1's. Wall-clock like search-v1, so it is the live opponent being measured. Against forge-default and search-v1 (J101).

players.name: search-v2-mull
players.note: D417: search-v2 (the ladder's search-v1-anytime) plus the opening-hand search, mull=1: at mulliganKeepHand keep is rolled out against mulligan, and at the London bottom Forge's cards against others, from the pre-game copy to game turn 6 (mullturns 3 a seat), 6 s a decision (mullms), overruling Forge only on the lcb rule (z 1, 3 paired rounds). Every other knob search-v2's. Fixed match against search-v1-anytime.

players.name: search-v2-targets
players.note: D417: search-v2 plus the target search, targets=1: when the seat's priority play (Forge's or the search's) has a part with one target, Forge's target is rolled out against up to 5 other legal ones (Forge's side first, then Forge's card value), on search-v2's own rule and budget. Fixed match against search-v1-anytime.

players.name: search-v2-mull-targets
players.note: D417: search-v2 with both switches, mull=1 and targets=1. Registered for a later match; J114 measures each switch alone.

players.name: search-v2-wlife50
players.note: D431: search-v2 (the ladder's search-v1-anytime) with the hand leaf's life curve term at 50% (x0.5), every other knob search-v2's. One of J125's eight coordinate steps: tuned on the dev set against search-v1-anytime; the best one is confirmed in a fixed match on the confirm set.
